items.title: Nvidia shares fall as probe into CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to alleged Chinese spy raises questions
items.desc: An internal investigation into whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation has put his future at the chipmaker under scrutiny, while his daughter cancels a planned visit to South Korea.

items.title: Landslides block Prithvi Highway, disrupting Tihar travel
items.desc: Travellers heading home for Tihar celebrations face delays after repeated landslides block the highway in Chitwan, with crews working to reopen both lanes by 1pm.

items.title: How many Nepalis are one flood away from poverty?
items.desc: Bhotekoshi flood pushed poverty up 2.7 percentage points. Prevention, not just relief, must be the answer.

items.title: From traditional songs to modern celebrations, Tihar is changing with the times and a new generation
items.desc: Traditional games and rituals are fading, celebrations are taking new forms, and younger Nepalis are questioning long-held social norms while embracing more environmentally conscious ways of marking the festival.

items.title: The two Nepali border villages that empty for six months every year
items.desc: Residents of Chhangru and Tinkar in Darchula move to lower elevations each winter to escape heavy snowfall and extreme cold, returning in spring after preparing their homes, fields and livestock for the long absence.

items.title: Six injured in jeep crash in Dailekh
items.desc: A vehicle carrying two patients and their attendants from Kalikot to Surkhet veered off the road at Kafaltoli on Monday morning.

items.title: Trump says he is highly unlikely to order Iran strikes if talks progress
items.desc: Trump says Washington will explore a diplomatic solution if talks make progress, but warns that Iran’s demands remain unacceptable as attacks on shipping continue in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Can Nepal cook dal bhat on its own electricity?
items.desc: Nepal spends tens of billions of rupees a year on cooking gas. A 10-year electric-cooking mission could cut the bill, starting with households, hotels and the grid.

items.title: Q&A: Before we get high on the cannabis law, let’s measure the plant
items.desc: Dr Amrit Baral says Gandaki’s cannabis law is a welcome start but argues it still lacks the science, standards and public education to work.

items.title: Top-four race goes down to the wire as NPL Season 3 nears league-stage conclusion
items.desc: With defending champions Lumbini Lions leading the pack, six franchises remain in mathematical contention for playoff qualification.

items.title: Three in four transport jobs in Nepal are informal
items.desc: ILO study calls for stronger labour protections, affordable social security contributions, and a legal framework to protect ride-hailing and delivery workers.

items.title: Nepal launches TikTok campaign to promote tourism to global audiences
items.desc: The campaign, running until the end of 2026, aims to showcase Nepal’s natural beauty, cultural heritage and diverse tourism experiences through digital storytelling and international content creators.

items.title: Nepal’s game developers seek tax relief, Google access to scale globally
items.desc: Industry leaders say high taxes and restrictions on Google Play merchant accounts are stifling local developers, as the prime minister pledges to create conditions for a home-grown technology unicorn.

items.title: Nepal’s share market weathers political jitters
items.desc: Rumours of a possible arrest of a top politician, business figures in custody, and the Tihar festive season rattled investors, but technical indicators suggest the market is regaining some stability.

items.title: Nepal’s peak electricity demand hits 1,813MW on Laxmi Puja evening
items.desc: The country exported 587.3MW of surplus power to India, while electricity supply remained uninterrupted nationwide during peak hours.

items.title: Nepal expects peak electricity demand to reach 1,700MW on Laxmi Puja
items.desc: The Nepal Electricity Authority says domestic generation will be sufficient to meet demand during Tihar, with industries expected to remain closed and power exports continuing.

items.title: Nepal clinch U-19 women’s cricket title unbeaten in China
items.desc: The four-team Belt and Road Series saw Nepal win four of their six matches, with the remaining two abandoned due to rain.

items.title: Poland mourns victims of Krakow mass shooting as security fears grow
items.desc: The 24-year-old suspect’s parents and sister were ​later found dead at their home, and he remained in hospital in a critical condition.

items.title: How Nepali artists are celebrating Tihar
items.desc: From buying silverware and festive essentials to writing screenplays and mourning loved ones, Nepali artists have different ways of marking—or sitting out—Tihar.

items.title: Jijivisha stitched Everest onto a red-carpet suit. Nothing came from Paris, Milan or New York.
items.desc: Designer Shavona Shrestha’s clothing label made an ivory silk suit for Thinley Lhamo to wear at the premiere of ‘Tenzing’, using Nepali silk, stones and artisans. It is the label’s boldest argument yet for Nepali couture.

items.title: Rinku Thakur turned her fight against child marriage into a mission
items.desc: After refusing an arranged marriage at 17 and leaving home, the Birgunj woman has spent over a decade raising awareness about child marriage, dowry, and women’s rights across Madhesh villages.

items.title: How China’s clean-tech machine is reshaping the global climate fight
items.desc: China’s clean-tech exports and investments in developing countries are approaching the scale of climate finance provided by wealthy nations, making its manufacturing industry a major force in the global energy transition.

items.title: From flood-hit areas to crime scenes, Nepal’s police dogs sniff out vital clues
items.desc: One of 107 dogs in the police force, Leo located two bodies and human remains during a 20-day search after the Bhotekoshi floods.

items.title: Nepal’s 250-year-old foreign policy still works. Why does no one use it?
items.desc: Nepal has drifted between Delhi and Beijing for three decades. The Shah government has the mandate to stop it.

items.title: Why this government still needs questioning
items.desc: The government moves at a rocket’s pace. Citizens should check the law behind the headlines before applauding.

items.title: The families who wait
items.desc: Remittances keep Nepal’s economy afloat. The people left behind carry a cost that rarely appears in figures.

items.title: Sugar supplies assured for Tihar, but LPG shortages persist
items.desc: Government agencies and traders say stocks of sugar and other food staples are sufficient to meet festival demand, even as problems with LPG distribution continue.

items.title: New Zealand preliminary vote leaves unclear who will govern
items.desc: The National-led coalition holds 67 seats in a projected 131-seat parliament, just above the majority threshold, but 14 percent of votes remain uncounted and could alter the balance.
